newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut t-bill issue raises 462.7 bln pounds.
newsitem.headline: Beirut t-bill issue raises 462.7 bln pounds.

text.p: Lebanon's weekly treasury bill issue of April 10 raised 462.7 billion Lebanese pounds, according to finance ministry results issued on Monday.
The previous issue raised 327.8 billion pounds.
The issue posted a nominal surplus of subscription against maturity of 92.7 billion pounds. It raised the following amounts (in billion of pounds, previous week in brackets):

The central bank said only 17 percent of all competitive bids -- those made by Lebanese institutions -- were accepted up to the discount rate and yield for three-month bills and 16 percent for six-month bills.

The Bank also restricted the acceptance of non-competitive bids -- those made by private individuals and foreign investors -- for three- and six-month bills. It approved only 17 percent up to the discount rate and yield for three-month bills and 16 percent for six-month bills.
However, all competitive and non-competitive bids were accepted for the 12-month and 24-month bills, the Bank said.
Last week, the bank approved only 14 percent of non-competitive bids up to the discount rate and yield for three-month bills and 16 percent for six-month bills.
The Lebanese pound closed at 1,544.75 to the U.S. dollar on Monday from 1,545.25 a week earlier and 1,581 a year ago.
